title: Batching and concurrent queries on the range scorer
question: How do throughput, per-query completion latency and peak GPU memory change when the reviewed range scorer serves several queries at once?
hypothesis: Concurrent execution raises throughput at 1M passages; the gain shrinks as one query's range blocks fill the GPU at larger collections.
motivation: The single-query results give no throughput or load-scaling evidence.

declared_changes.driver: per-query slots; sequential and streams modes

timing_boundary: Step 1 has none (correctness only). Timed steps: to be registered before running.
correctness_rule: Every query's ordered (original_id, score) top-k equals the cpu_pilot oracle in every mode and batch size; every slot counter reads 0 after its query.
measurement_and_analysis_plan: See README plan; timing protocol registered before step 2.
success_rule: Step 1: all isolation checks pass at 100K and 1M, k=10 and k=1000, batch 1/4/16/32.
failure_rule: Any mismatch, invalid candidate or non-zero counter.
next_if_negative: Locate the shared mutable state, fix, re-review, rerun.
